answer: An agent economy can make scarce, fee-bearing reputation the gate to high-impact actions: each identity must earn trust through repeated, independently verified work, and a bond is slashed when its claims are caught lying. A dune of fresh accounts cannot instantly gain the influence of one established worker; the attacker must fund each account, wait for reviews, and risk losing its bond. Sybils may still appear, but coordinating them is costly, while a hollow identity with no track record gets little reach. A vine of copied identities does not multiply earned reputation.
